signals.title: USD/CAD — Geopolitical Shock + Trade Breakdown
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3784 following the collapse of US-Canada trade talks and the implementation of 50% tariffs. The breakdown reintroduces significant cross-border trade risk into North American markets, complicating the outlook for CAD despite its positive ESI index of +24.9. Technically, the pair is holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3954, 1.4061, 1.3843), reflecting recent CAD strength that is now under threat from trade retaliation. Fed 3.75% vs BoC 2.25% provides a +150bp carry advantage for the USD, which typically supports the pair during periods of regional trade friction. The trade shock acts as a primary headwind that could force a repricing of the CAD long trade. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; tariff escalation overrides recent CAD data outperformance. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Rapid resolution of trade talks or de-escalation of tariff rhetoric from the US administration.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF is at 0.5738 as the G10 scorecard highlights a 1.051% spread between the week's leader and laggard. AUD 1W avg outperformance of +0.772% is supported by a significant carry advantage, with RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0% offering a +435bp spread. CHF remains the G10 laggard with a 1W avg of -0.279%, pressured by the absence of risk-off flows while VIX remains at 15.1. Retail sentiment on the cross is at a 89% short extreme, providing a contrarian tailwind for further AUD appreciation as retail fades the carry trend. This bilateral theme remains dominant as long as global volatility stays contained. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage favors the G10 leader vs the yield laggard. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: VIX spikes above 25, triggering a rapid safe-haven bid for CHF and a carry unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry + Options Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.78 remains supported by a +275bp carry premium (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%) despite recent price softening. Volatility markets exhibit unusual complacency with USD/JPY IV at 7.2% vs HV30 of 8.8%, resulting in a negative vol risk premium (VRP) of -1.6%. The 25d RR at -1.96 confirms a strong put skew, indicating that while spot remains bid on carry, institutional players are paying for downside protection. COT LF net short JPY at -73,641 shows the carry trade is established but no longer at 52-week extremes (pctl 38). The JPY safe-haven function appears impaired as USD/JPY vs VIX correlation holds at +0.434 (z=+2.09σ). Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance persists while VIX remains in normal volatility range. Catalyst: Next BoJ meeting — hike bias priced. BoJ holds at 1.0%.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Institutional Skew + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3653, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3485, 1.3395, 1.3427). The options market is pricing in significant protection with a +5.1% vol risk premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 5.9%), suggesting expected volatility far exceeds recent realized moves. COT LF net long GBP at +46,070 is nearing crowded territory at pctl 94, z+1.45, while the 25d RR remains neutral at -0.06. This suggests that despite the spot rally to 6.5-month highs, institutions are reluctant to add directional call exposure at these levels. ESI for GBP is moderately negative at -8.3, providing a fundamental divergence to the bullish technical setup. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; high vol premium and crowded longs suggest limited upside without a fresh macro catalyst. Catalyst: Next BoE meeting — 100% hold priced. Risk: Sharp USD recovery on US fiscal outlook concerns forces a GBP long unwind toward the SMA cluster.
